object_description: eight-storey staggered volume with continuous closed parapet bands around a three-storey top-lit hall
design_condition: the volume continues the accentuating row of buildings along the street by taking up the height of the two existing high-rises, staggering its structure to respond to the varied neighbouring heights

positive: The project continues the urban idea of the site, seen as a unified building area
It takes up the height of the two existing high-rise buildings along the street
The accentuating row of buildings at the foot of the slope is meaningfully continued
The staggered structure responds to the surrounding neighbours with its different heights
Despite its self-confident eight storeys it blends in well with the nearby built environment
The continuous closed parapet bands sensibly continue the theme of the staggered structure
Ribbed ceramic panels with aluminium window strips create an elegant architectural image
This can be read as a reference to the main buildings, continuing the ensemble character
The limited surrounding space is sensibly supplemented with two large outdoor terraces on sunlit upper floors
The strategy of compensating for missing outdoor space is consistently continued inside
A large three-storey hall with zenithal lighting becomes the heart and identification point
Differently sized, well-proportioned classrooms are arranged on three floors around this hall
The learning landscapes are connected to the air space of the hall as terraces
Two open staircases in the hall lead to the upper floors and the basement laboratories
The spatial layout of the administration meets the requirements of the space allocation plan
Careful statics and system separation suggest an economical and sustainable solution
Precise urban design and building form blend well with the heterogeneous environment
The relationship to the development structure of the site is not lost
The central identity-creating hall, functional structure and two elevated terraces are a promising contribution
negative: The resulting individual building sections are still too unbalanced in relation to the overall structure
There is no generous spatial connection to the inner access area of the basement
That connection would also have lit the now unattractive zone
The mezzanine floor lacks a more spacious connection to the shared hall space
A more attractive spatial connection to the shared terrace would further strengthen the project
The administration does not allow a communicative working environment for all areas
There is no connection between the internal access area and the shared outdoor space
The volume has a very large floor area and the largest facade area
The lower proportion of glass cannot compensate for the otherwise unfavourable surface ratios
Construction costs are at the upper end of the competition
Arranging the administration on four storeys makes the desired communicative working environment impossible
